record.paper_title: Some open problems on best approximation in normed linear spaces
record.context_brief: Topological characterization for finite-dimensional Chebyshev subspaces of complex C(Q)
record.original_question: Characterize, in purely topological terms, the compact spaces Q for which the complex Banach space C(Q) of continuous complex-valued functions on Q with the supremum norm contains a finite-dimensional Chebyshev subspace of dimension n > 1. Equivalently, characterize the compact spaces Q that admit a complex Chebyshev system x1, ..., xn with n > 1, meaning that every nontrivial linear combination of these functions has at most n - 1 zeros on Q.

evidence.quote: Characterize (topologically) those compact spaces Q for which the complex space C(Q) (of all continuous functions on Q with ||x|| = max |x(q)| ) contains a Cebysev subspace of finite dimension n > 1 .
Thus the above problem amounts to the following : Characterize (topologically) those compact spaces Q which admit a Cebysev system x1 , ... , xn with n > 1 .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Q$ be a compact Hausdorff space and let $C(Q)$ denote the complex Banach space of continuous complex-valued functions on $Q$ equipped with the supremum norm $\|x\| = \max_{q\in Q}|x(q)|$. A linear subspace $L\subset C(Q)$ is called a Chebyshev subspace if for every $f\in C(Q)$ there exists a unique element of $L$ that is a best approximation to $f$ in the supremum norm. Equivalently, an $n$-tuple of continuous complex-valued functions $x_1,\dots,x_n\in C(Q)$ is called a (complex) Chebyshev system on $Q$ if every nonzero complex linear combination $c_1 x_1 + \cdots + c_n x_n$ has at most $n-1$ zeros on $Q$; the span of such a system is a finite-dimensional Chebyshev subspace of $C(Q)$.

Problem: Give a purely topological characterization of those compact Hausdorff spaces $Q$ for which the complex Banach space $C(Q)$ contains a finite-dimensional Chebyshev subspace of dimension $n>1$; equivalently, characterize topologically those compact spaces $Q$ that admit a complex Chebyshev system $x_1,\dots,x_n$ with $n>1$.
artifact.status_search_result: Mairhuber-type theorems give a topological characterization in the real case (Q must be homeomorphic to a subset of a circle, with parity restrictions), but the complex setting behaves differently and a complete purely topological characterization of compact spaces Q admitting a complex Chebyshev system of dimension n>1 does not appear in the literature; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Chebyshev system - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Topological characterizations exist for real Chebyshev systems via Mairhuber-type theorems.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references address the real case; the complex analogue is not stated as resolved.

status_evidence.title: Chebyshev Alternation Theorem. Haar's and Mairhuber's Theorems
status_evidence.snippet: Mairhuber's theorem characterizes metrizable compact Q for which C(Q) has nontrivial finite-dimensional Chebyshev subspaces (real case).
status_evidence.claim: Topological characterization is known in the real case; the complex case differs and is not fully characterized.

status_evidence.title: Another look at Chebyshev systems (Zalik)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Chebyshev systems; complex case behaves differently from the real case.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates that the complex situation is more subtle and that a full topological characterization is not established.
